security_spec.violation_condition: If QEMU implements ACLIC extensions (Smaclic/Ssaclic/Smnip/Ssnip/Smehv) in the future but gates them on a hypothetical ext_smaiae flag that forces mvip/mvien read-only zero — as the old spec permitted — instead of requiring full ext_smaia/ext_ssaia with functional virtual interrupt CSRs, guest software relying on interrupt filtering through mvip/mvien will receive no interrupts on bits 1, 5, and 9, violating the updated dependency chain.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: ext_smaiae || Smaiae || smaiae — any ACLIC CSR registration (smclic/ssclic/smnip/ssnip/smehv) gated on a removed/non-existent Smaiae flag instead of the full Smaia/Ssaia flag, or mvip_writable_mask/mvien_writable_mask zeroed out when ACLIC features are active.
security_spec.summary: PR removes Smaiae (which forced xvip/xvien read-only zero) and promotes ACLIC dependency to full Smaia/Ssaia; QEMU must ensure future ACLIC CSR implementations validate ext_smaia/ext_ssaia with functional mvip/mvien, not the removed Smaiae subset.

findings.finding: M-mode AIA CSR access correctly gated on ext_smaia (not a removed ext_smaiae flag). No ACLIC sub-extensions are implemented, so no risk of gating them on a non-existent flag.
S-mode AIA CSR access correctly gated on ext_ssaia. Uses direct ext_ssaia check rather than any removed intermediate flag.

mvip_writable_mask and mvien_writable_mask are properly defined with functional interrupt bits (MIP_SSIP, MIP_STIP, MIP_SEIP, LOCAL_INTERRUPTS), not zeroed out. No ext_smaiae flag exists to force them to read-only zero.
rmw_mvip correctly applies mvip_writable_mask for both alias (forwarded to mip) and non-alias bits (stored in env->mvip). No forced read-only zero.
SMSTATEEN0 write mask correctly gates SMSTATEEN0_SVSLCT on ext_smaia || ext_smcsrind, and SMSTATEEN0_AIA/IMSIC on ext_smaia alone. Uses the real ext_smaia flag, not a removed ext_smaiae.
MIREG access gated on ext_smaia, SIREG/VSIREG on ext_ssaia. All correct direct checks — no ext_smaiae intermediate flag.
